name: Hananiah
overview: Hananiah was a male Levite and a descendant of Aaron, serving as a priest. He is identified specifically as the son of Jeremiah in Nehemiah 12:12, situating him within the priestly lineage of the tribe of Levi. His role as a priest highlights his participation in the religious life of Israel during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Hananiah means "Yahweh is gracious," reflecting a common theophoric element in Hebrew names that acknowledges God's grace. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:12, does not indicate it was given directly by God but carries significant spiritual meaning consistent with Israelite naming practices.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hananiah as the son of Jeremiah, as noted in Nehemiah 12:12. Beyond this paternal relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text concerning Hananiah.
scriptureSignificance: Hananiah's significance lies in his identification as a priest descended from Aaron, emphasizing the continuity of the Levitical priesthood during the restoration of Israel following the exile. His mention in Nehemiah 12:12 connects him to the efforts of reestablishing proper worship and temple service, underscoring the faithfulness of God's covenant people in maintaining their sacred duties.
